note: What we're hearing — competitor mentions aggregated from Gong across open opportunities. Patterns and counts only. Never a customer name, a contact name, a deal name, or a verbatim quote. Generated by the weekly Gong sweep; human-editable via the admin sheet.
source: Gong, via CRM opportunities in Demo/Solution Evaluation
excluded: Ellis Partners appeared in 2 deals as an incumbent being replaced by PerformanceHQ. Ellis is a Grace Hill company, so this is an internal migration, not a competitive loss. Excluded from the counts below.

realpage-realconnect.posture: Incumbent in both — already installed, not a fresh evaluation.
whatBuyersSay: Described as adequate for basic delivery, but unable to record attendance, run quizzes, or hold anyone accountable for instructor-led sessions.
The calendar does not carry hosting links or push notifications, so teams track sessions manually and re-enter the same data twice.
Buyers running it alongside a second system want to consolidate rather than add a third login.
objectionsToUs: Concern about confusing onsite teams with a second training program and another login when a RealPage LMS is already deployed.
realpage-realconnect.pricingSignal: One buyer expects RealPage costs to rise as AI features are added, and reports being pushed toward more services after a prior platform investment. Cost reduction was named as a reason to look elsewhere.
realpage-realconnect.confirms: Matches the record's gap that RealPage does not publish what is actually in the library. The field adds specifics the product page omits: attendance, assessment and instructor-led tracking.
realpage-realconnect.useIt: Do not attack the platform. Ask what happens after a session ends — who records attendance, who proves competency, and how many places that data gets typed.

microsoft-sharepoint.posture: Incumbent storage, not a vendor evaluation.
whatBuyersSay: Policy and form versions scatter across sites, so new hires and existing staff both struggle to find the current one.
Used together with Teams for tracking, with the manual work involved described as unreasonable.
One buyer running Microsoft Forms for onboarding and exit surveys called it badly out of date and limited in how surveys can be configured.
microsoft-sharepoint.pricingSignal: None raised. It is already paid for, which is the whole difficulty.
microsoft-sharepoint.confirms: Exactly the displacement conversation the record describes — the fight is over version control and acknowledgment evidence, never document storage.
microsoft-sharepoint.useIt: Let them keep it for files. Ask who writes and updates the policy text today, and whether they could produce a timestamped acknowledgment per employee per version at audit.

status-quo-policies.posture: No vendor in the deal at all.
whatBuyersSay: A 250-page manual that nobody opens on the job.
Training passed on by word of mouth, inconsistently.
Fair housing delivered by outside counsel, not annually, with little retention afterward.
Paper-based policy and HR books that are hard to reach when someone needs them.
status-quo-policies.pricingSignal: The status quo is free, so every conversation is a value case rather than a price comparison.
status-quo-policies.confirms: The status quo remains the most common thing we are actually replacing — more common in this sample than any named vendor.
status-quo-policies.useIt: Do not sell against the binder. Ask what happens when someone needs the answer at 4pm on a Friday, and how they would prove today what a departed employee was taught.

eliseai.posture: Deployed for phone handling alongside the evaluation.
whatBuyersSay: Regional managers report frustration with results and with how follow-up is tracked.
A mystery shopper has to explicitly ask for a live person to get past the assistant.
eliseai.confirms: Supports the shopping angle — an AI answering layer changes what a shop is measuring, and creates a new thing to measure.
eliseai.useIt: Not a competitor here. Ask how they currently verify what the AI says to a prospect, and who owns the handoff when it escalates to a person.

appfolio-staffing-training.posture: The buyer's PMS, raised as a possible source of training content.
whatBuyersSay: Described as having an extensive library, with an implication that existing PMS resources might cover the need.
objectionsToUs: Implicit: why buy training when the PMS already includes some.
appfolio-staffing-training.confirms: The free-module objection is live in AppFolio accounts, as the record predicts.
appfolio-staffing-training.useIt: Agree it is useful and tell them to keep it. Ask which of those courses carries CE credit, which is state-approved for fair housing, and who updates them when the law changes.
